_comment: Authored attack trees for LINCHPIN, rooted in the threat model. scripts/check-attack-trees.py validates them against .agent/verification/state/THREAT_MODEL.json and the tree (every leaf must cite a modelled threat, every MITIGATED leaf must name a symbol that exists, every OPEN or PARTIAL leaf must name the decision or residual that keeps it open) and renders .agent/evidence/attack-trees.md. Edit here, never in the rendered document.

scope.product: LINCHPIN -- local-first Windows patent-intelligence desktop application
scope.method: goal-first attack trees in the Schneier sense: a root adversarial goal decomposed into AND/OR refinements, with each leaf either mitigated by a named control (bound to a symbol that must exist) or left OPEN/PARTIAL with the decision that keeps it that way

trees.goal: exfiltrate the invention content from the device
trees.comment: The highest-value goal for this product: the disclosure is the asset. Three independent routes are considered, and the tree is an OR because any one of them suffices for the attacker.

nodes.description: route the content off-device through the provider boundary
point the product at a remote inference endpoint and let it send prompts there
nodes.evidence: the endpoint is validated before any I/O and a non-loopback host is refused with POLICY, with no attempt made; the refusal is asserted at both the transport and the product-command layer, and the same negative runs against the packaged executable

nodes.description: exploit a credentialed remote lane once one is wired
nodes.evidence: no credentialed provider lane exists in this architecture, so neither the egress nor the credential-failure behaviour of one has been executed
nodes.residual: DOD-014 is PARTIAL for exactly this reason: the pack's governance (terms review) precedes any provider integration, and wiring a lane is an owner decision under change control

nodes.description: capture the content in something the product writes down
have a credential or invention fragment land in telemetry, diagnostics or an incident capsule
nodes.evidence: redaction runs on the diagnostics path before storage, an induced failure is asserted to carry its correlation id with a planted credential absent from every recorded detail, and the capsule export guard refuses a surviving registered secret

nodes.description: export a filing package or evidence bundle that carries restricted content
nodes.evidence: the export gateway refuses restricted content, the support matrix refuses a package whose limitations are unanchored, and a package never claims a document format the product cannot produce

nodes.description: leave unlabelled secret material in free text that the redactor cannot attribute to a key or token shape
nodes.evidence: the redactor removes values it can attribute to a key name or a known token shape, and a property-style test covers punctuation-wrapped and quoted forms
nodes.residual: a secret pasted with no key name and no recognisable shape is not detectable by either layer; stated as a residual in the threat model rather than claimed closed

nodes.description: read the vault from the filesystem
read the vault file directly as the logged-in user or as malware running with the user's rights
nodes.evidence: the vault is a device-local SQLite database with content-addressed blobs; workspace scoping and the audit chain are asserted, but the file is readable by anything running as the user
nodes.residual: no OS-encrypted container exists and the only KeyringStore is an in-process map -- the product's own scope map (UO-01) states this limitation, and the threat model records it as accepted risk R-2

nodes.description: reach the vault through a path or archive traversal from a crafted import
nodes.evidence: path and archive-entry hardening rejects absolute paths and traversal, verified by a property test over a generated corpus and by a mutation proof that removes the guard

trees.goal: destroy or forge the conception record
trees.comment: For a patent workflow the record of who conceived what is the product's output; destroying it is a denial of the user's rights, and forging it is worse.

nodes.description: destroy the durable state
corrupt or delete the vault and its WAL siblings
nodes.evidence: the recovery drill injects total loss and in-place corruption repeatedly, recovers through the production command, and reconciles the recovered state by content digest through an independent connection with measured RPO/RTO against an enforced threshold

nodes.description: make a restore silently replace live state with an empty database
nodes.evidence: a mistyped backup path is refused instead of created, the destination is recreated and quarantined when missing, and every recovery is reconciled by digest

nodes.description: forge or rewrite the record without detection
edit the audit chain after the fact
nodes.evidence: the audit chain is hash-chained and a test tampers with a stored entry and asserts detection

nodes.description: present AI-generated content as human conception
nodes.evidence: conception events carry an origin label that cannot be conflated, and the ledger read separates the two origins at the product boundary

trees.goal: get a tampered or unauthorised build installed and run
trees.comment: The distribution path carries no signature, so the tree concentrates on what IS checked.

nodes.description: substitute the artefact in transit or at rest
swap the executable for one that opens a debug port and leaks through it
nodes.evidence: the production artifact is asserted to open no debug port, with the probe baseline-checked, pid-attributed and liveness-checked so a dead process cannot pass vacuously

nodes.description: ship a package whose payload is not the built binary
nodes.evidence: the installed executable is bound to the digest of the payload the MSI itself carries (extracted with msiexec /a), which is what exposed the bundler relinking the binary during packaging

nodes.description: distribute through a compromised channel
nodes.evidence: digests are published and verified out of band, and the build is reproducible, but nothing binds authorship
nodes.residual: the release is UNSIGNED (ADR-003): a digest proves integrity against an out-of-band value, not authorship; accepted risk R-1

threat_notes.why: spoofing reduces to capability grants and file access here: there is no identity surface to spoof (measured: zero login/session/role constructs), and a granted capability is what decides whether a client may act, which is a control rather than an attack route of its own
repudiation of conception is the forging branch of AT-2: the origin label and the audit chain are the two controls that decide it
prompt egress to a remote host is the first branch of AT-1; the loopback-only guard is the same control seen from the provider side
denial of service against the vault is the destruction branch of AT-2, where the fault-injected recovery drill and the encoded latency/throughput floors are the controls
traversal out of the evidence directory is the escape branch of AT-1's filesystem route; the hardening property test is the control
a secret captured by diagnostics or an incident capsule is the capture branch of AT-1; the redaction and capsule-export guards are the controls

threat_notes.coverage: no tree: dependency compromise is a supply-chain path whose controls (locked graphs, advisory and ban scanning, SBOM currency, secret scan, clean build) are policy gates rather than steps an attacker takes against this host, and none of them is an attack leaf the user can be walked through

threat_notes.why: over-disclosure through an export is the export branch of AT-1; the firewall, support matrix and document-format assertions are the controls
